cards.b: Random-access memory. Volatile main memory that holds the programs and data currently in use. Can be read and written.
Read-only memory. Non-volatile; stores the start-up (boot) instructions. Normally only read.
Loses its contents when the power is turned off. RAM is volatile; ROM and secondary storage are not.
Small, very fast memory near the CPU holding frequently used instructions and data. Faster but smaller than RAM.
Part of secondary storage used as if it were RAM when RAM is full. Allows more programs to run, but is much slower.
Data stored as magnetised areas on spinning platters (hard disk drive). Cheap per GB, large capacity, but has moving parts.
A laser reads pits and lands on a disc (CD, DVD, Blu-ray). Cheap and portable, but low capacity and easily scratched.
Flash memory with no moving parts (SSD, USB stick, SD card). Fast, silent, durable, low power, but dearer per GB.
Needs an internet connection, may cost a subscription, security and privacy risks, and depends on the provider.
Manages files, processes and memory, hardware (device drivers), the user interface (GUI or command line), and security.
Software that lets the operating system communicate with and control a particular hardware device.
Rearranges the fragments of files on a hard disk so each file is stored together, making access faster. Not needed for SSDs.
System software runs and manages the computer (OS, utilities). Application software lets users do tasks (word processor, browser).
High-level: English-like, portable, easier to write and debug. Low-level (machine code, assembly): close to hardware, processor-specific, harder to write.
Compiler translates the whole program to an executable before running (fast). Interpreter translates and runs line by line (stops at first error, slower).

short.q: State two differences between RAM and ROM.
short.model: RAM is volatile and ROM is non-volatile. RAM can be read from and written to, while ROM is normally read-only and holds the boot program.
points: read/write vs read only (or purpose: data in use vs boot program)

short.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of using an SSD instead of a hard disk drive.
short.model: An SSD has no moving parts so it is faster, quieter and more durable. However it costs more per gigabyte.
points: advantage: faster / no moving parts / durable / silent

short.q: Describe what is meant by an operating system and give two of its functions.
short.model: An operating system is system software that manages the hardware and software of a computer and provides a user interface. For example it manages files and shares processor time between running programs.
points: system software that manages hardware/software and gives a user interface
two functions e.g. file management, process/memory management, device drivers

short.q: Give two reasons why a programmer might choose a high-level language rather than a low-level language.
short.model: High-level languages are easier to read, write and debug because they are close to English. They are also portable, so the same program can be translated to run on different processors.

short.q: A developer is testing a new program. Explain why an interpreter might be more useful than a compiler during testing.
short.model: An interpreter runs the program line by line and stops at the first error, so the developer can find and fix errors immediately and re-run without a full compile each time.
points: translates and runs line by line / stops at the first error
easy to find and fix errors quickly
